arguments.title: 5 Smart Ways to Prepare Your Business for Funding in 2026
arguments.subtitle: A quick checklist for business owners seeking capital
arguments.content:
Why Preparation Matters

Lenders evaluate more than just your credit score. A well-prepared application signals that you run a serious operation and dramatically improves your approval odds.

1. Organize Your Financial Statements

Have your last three months of bank statements, profit and loss statements, and balance sheets ready. Digital copies are fine — most lenders accept PDF uploads.

2. Know Your Numbers Cold

Be ready to state your monthly revenue, average daily balance, and debt obligations without hesitation. Inconsistency raises red flags.

3. Choose the Right Funding Type

Revenue-based financing suits businesses with strong daily sales. Equipment financing secures machinery purchases. SBA loans offer the lowest rates for established businesses with patience for underwriting.

4. Check Your Credit Before Applying

Pull your personal and business credit reports. Address any errors. A 680+ score opens most doors. Below 600, focus on revenue-based options.

5. Have a Clear Use of Funds

Lenders want specifics — inventory purchase, hiring, marketing campaign, renovation. "Working capital" is too vague. Tie every dollar to a concrete outcome.
